content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2 (cancel 15:30-16:00 coaching plus 20% chat deflection 15:00-16:00) for ₹1,491, and bring in the duty manager: it lifts 13:30-15:30 service level only to 53.1% against an 80% target.","why":"The problem is long calls, not extra volume. Handle time on general has risen to 646 s against about 350–376 s forecast, in line with P2 incident INC-20261021-5862 (CRM customer search taking 20–40 s). Volume and staffing are close to plan. With no action, service level over 13:30-15:30 is predicted at 47.2% with 14.6% abandons. P2 raises it to 53.1% (payments 61.5%, general 43.3%) and cuts abandons to 13.0%. Rest of day improves from 79.2% to 81.2%. It is the best plan that breaks no policy rule. No plan reaches 80%, and 53% is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02), so the duty manager should be involved. The real fix is resolving the CRM incident, and they may need to push that or authorise stronger measures.","trade_offs":["P0 and P1 cost nothing but leave service level at about 47% (P1 is 47.0%, so the break reshuffle and callbacks add nothing).","P3 costs the same ₹1,491 as P2 but predicts slightly worse: 52.6% vs 53.1%.","R1 and R2 predict 53.8%, with general at 47.3% and 11.9% abandons, and R2 is cheaper at ₹1,215. Both break CX-01 because the known-issue message targets refund_status on payments, which is not rising.","P2 mostly helps payments (61.5%). General stays weak at 43.3% because that is where the slow CRM hurts most."],"watch":"Watch general handle time and the CRM incident status. If search speed recovers, handle time should fall back toward 350–376 s. If it stays near 646 s, general will stay around 43% and the duty manager should decide on further action. Also check that the chat deflection is actually taking volume from 15:00."}
